title: CloseAllApplications
description: Do necessary procedures for ending the process (e.g., logout) and close the applications used in the process.

title: GetCredentials
description:
Securely fetch or create and use a set of credentials.

First, there is an attempt to fetch credentials from Orchestrator using the name received as argument. 
If it is not possible to retrieve those credentials from Orchestrator, there is an attempt to fetch them from the Windows Credential Manager (WCM). 
If the credentials are not defined in the WCM, the user is prompted to create the credentials that will be added to the WCM and returned for use during the process execution.

The Private property is used to prevent the generation of logs that might contain information about the credentials.

in_Credential.description: Name of the credential to be retrieved.

out_Username.description: Username associated with the specified credential.

out_Password.description: Password associated with the specified credential.

title: GetTransactionData
description:
Get a transaction item from a specified source (e.g., spreadsheets, databases, email, web API or Orchestrator). 

If there are no transaction items remaining, out_TransactionItem is set to Nothing, which leads to the End Process state. 

For cases in which there is only a single transaction (i.e., a linear process), check whether the argument in_TransactionNumber has the value 1 (meaning it's the first and only transaction) and assign the transaction item to out_TransactionItem. For any other value of in_TransactionNumber, out_TransactionItem should be set to Nothing.

If there are multiple transactions, use the argument in_TransactionNumber as an index to retrieve the correct transaction to be processed. If there are no more transactions left, it is necessary to set out_TransactionItem to Nothing, thus ending the process.

in_Config.description: Dictionary structure to store configuration data.

io_TransactionData.description: This variable can be used in case transactions are stored in a DataTable (for example, after being retrieved from a spreadsheet).

out_TransactionField1.description: Allow the optional addition of information about the transaction item.

out_TransactionField2.description: Allow the optional addition of information about the transaction item.

out_TransactionID.description: Transaction ID used for information and logging purposes. Ideally, the ID should be unique for each transaction.

idempotency.scope: taking an item marks it In Progress, so a retry takes the next one

title: Initialize Applications
description: Open applications used in the process and do necessary initialization procedures (e.g., login).

in_Config.description:
Dictionary structure to store configuration data. This structure can be used to store, for example, an URL for a system that needs to be initialized. 
It is not recommended to use it to store credentials; instead, store them on Orchestrator and just pass the name of the credential asset as a setting in this dictionary. Then use the GetAppCredentials workflow to retrieve the credentials securely.

title: InitiAllSettings
description:
Initialize, populate and output a configuration Dictionary to be used throughout the project. 
Settings and constants are read from the local configuration file, and assets are fetched from Orchestrator. 
Asset values will overwrite settings and constant values if they are defined with the same name.

in_ConfigFile.description: Path to the configuration file that defines settings, constants and assets.

in_ConfigSheets.description: Names of the sheets corresponding to settings and constants in the configuration file.

out_Config.description: Dictionary that holds values of settings, constants and assets.

title: KillAllProcesses
description:
Use the Kill Process activity to force the termination of the Windows processes representing applications used in the business process.
Note that killing processes might have undesired outcomes, like losing unsaved changes to files.

title: SetTransactionStatus
description:
Set and log the transaction's status along with extra log fields. 
There can be three possible statuses: Success, Business Rule Exception and System Error (Application Exception).

Business Rule Exception characterizes an irregular situation according to the process's rules and prevents the transaction to be processed. The transaction is not retried in this case, since the result will be the same until the problem that causes the exception is solved.
For example, it can be considered a BusinessRuleException if a process expects to read an email's attachment, but the sender didn't attach any file. In this case, immediate retries of the transaction will not yield a different result.

On the other hand, system errors are characterized by exceptions whose types are different than BusinessRuleException. When this kind of exception happens, the transaction item can be retried after closing and reopening the applications involved in the process. The rationale behind this is that the exception was caused by a problem in the applications, which might be solved by restarting them.

If Orchestrator queues are the source of transactions, the Set Transaction Status activity is used to update the status. In addition, the retry mechanism is also implemented by Orchestrator.

If Orchestrator queues are not used, the status can be set, for example, by writing to a specific column in a spreadsheet. In such cases, the retry mechanism is covered by the framework and the number of retries is defined in the configuration file.

At the end, io_TransactionNumber is incremented, which makes the framework get the next transaction to be processed.

in_Config.description: Dictionary structure to store configuration data.

in_SystemError.description: Exception variable that is used during transitions between states.

in_BusinessRuleException.description: Exception variable that is used during transitions between states.

io_RetryNumber.description: This variable controls the number of attempts of retrying the process in case of System Error.

in_TransactionField1.description: Allow the optional addition of information about the transaction item.

in_TransactionField2.description: Allow the optional addition of information about the transaction item.

in_TransactionID.description: Transaction ID used for information and logging purposes.

idempotency.scope: one final status per queue item

title: TakeScreenshot
description:
Capture a screenshot, log its name and location and save it with the PNG extension.
If no specific filepath is passed as argument, it'll save the image in the folder specified by in_Folder.

in_Folder.description: Path to the folder where the screenshot should be saved.

io_FilePath.description: Optional argument that specifies the path and the name of the screenshot to be taken.

title: Main
description: Process supplier invoices from the AP_Invoices queue: take each item, book it in the ERP and set its status in Orchestrator.

in_OrchestratorQueueName.description: Allows the Orchestrator queue name to be passed as an argument, instead of only being defined in the configuration file.

idempotency.scope: the queue; items already processed are never taken again

title: Process
description:
Invoke major steps of the business process, which are usually implemented by different workflows.

If a BusinessRuleException is thrown, the transaction will be skipped. 
If another kind of exception (ApplicationException) occurs, the current transaction can be retried.

in_Config.description: Dictionary structure to store configuration data.

title: TryCatch
description:
Securely fetch or create and use a set of credentials.

First, there is an attempt to fetch credentials from Orchestrator using the name received as argument. 
If it is not possible to retrieve those credentials from Orchestrator, there is an attempt to fetch them from the Windows Credential Manager (WCM). 
If the credentials are not defined in the WCM, the user is prompted to create the credentials that will be added to the WCM and returned for use during the process execution.

The Private property is used to prevent the generation of logs that might contain information about the credentials.

x-xaml-template.xml:
<TryCatch DisplayName="Private: Get Application Credentials">
  <TryCatch.Variables>
    <Variable x:TypeArguments="x:String" Name="StringPassword" />
  </TryCatch.Variables>
  <TryCatch.Try>

        </ActivityAction.Argument>
        <!-- activities -->
      </ActivityAction>
    </Catch>
  </TryCatch.Catches>

</TryCatch>
